questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Fill up: Pfannenstiel incision is placed ______ and its feature is ______.
opts: a finger-breadth above the symphysis pubis; cosmetic, rectus muscle not cut
a finger-breadth above the symphysis pubis; poor cosmetic result, rectus muscle cut
3 cm below the ASIS line; cosmetic, rectus muscle not cut
3 cm below the ASIS line; poor cosmetic result, rectus muscle cut
questions.exp: The Pfannenstiel incision sits a finger breadth above the pubic symphysis (low transverse); it is cosmetically good and the rectus muscle is not cut. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Which of the following statements about Joel-Cohen incision compared with Pfannenstiel is TRUE?
opts: Joel-Cohen is straight rather than curved and sited about 3 cm below the line joining the ASIS
Joel-Cohen is curved rather than straight and sited lower close to the symphysis pubis
Joel-Cohen is a vertical midline incision carried down from the umbilicus to the symphysis
Joel-Cohen is a transverse incision placed at the level of the umbilicus with muscle cutting
questions.exp: Joel-Cohen is a straight, higher transverse incision with blunt dissection; Pfannenstiel is curved and lower with more dissection. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Which of the following statements about transverse skin incision for caesarean is TRUE?
opts: Transverse incision gives less pain, stronger wound and better cosmesis but limits upper abdomen view
Transverse incision gives faster entry but causes more postoperative pain and weaker wound
Transverse incision gives better pelvic exposure though the scar is cosmetically less acceptable
Transverse incision causes less bleeding but results in a mechanically weaker wound postoperatively
questions.exp: Transverse incisions heal better and hurt less, but they limit access to the upper abdomen compared with a vertical incision. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match the uterine incision with its description — 1) Sanger's 2) Kerr's 3) Kronig's … A) Classical upper segment vertical B) Lower segment transverse C) Low vertical
questions.exp: Sanger's is the classical vertical incision, Kerr's the standard lower segment transverse, and Kronig's a low vertical incision. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Fill up: Risk of scar rupture is ______ for classical caesarean and ______ for one previous LSCS.
questions.exp: Classical 4–9%; one LSCS 0.2–0.9%; multiple LSCS 0.9–1.8%; low vertical 1–7%. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match VBAC eligibility with scar type — 1) Classical 2) One previous LSCS 3) Low vertical (Kronig) … A) Contraindicated B) May be allowed with counselling C) May be allowed, indicated for constriction ring
questions.exp: VBAC contraindicated after classical; ± after LSCS or low vertical (Krönig indicated for constriction ring). (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: A 30-year-old woman with a previous classical caesarean at 28 weeks is counselled for the next pregnancy. She is now 36 weeks with no labour pains. What is the most appropriate plan regarding timing and mode?
opts: Repeat caesarean at 36-37 weeks, since contractions become prominent after 37 weeks and raise rupture risk
Trial of labour aiming for vaginal birth at 40 completed weeks with continuous CTG monitoring
Repeat classical section at 39 completed weeks after confirming fetal lung maturity by amniocentesis
Induction of labour at 38 weeks using prostaglandins followed by oxytocin augmentation
questions.exp: A classical scar ruptures silently and catastrophically, so delivery is planned at 36-37 weeks before strong contractions begin. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Which of the following statements about VBAC guidelines after lower segment caesarean is TRUE?
opts: ACOG says a trial may be offered whatever the number of scars; India says contraindicated with two or more
ACOG permits trial after one scar only; Indian guidelines permit trial after any number of scars
ACOG never offers a trial after any scar; India offers trial after two previous sections routinely
ACOG permits trial after three scars; India permits trial after one scar only with mandatory pelvimetry
questions.exp: ACOG allows a trial after any number of low transverse scars after counselling; Indian guidance treats two or more as a contraindication. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
questions.q: Match the caesarean incision with its description — 1) Pfannenstiel incision 2) Joel-Cohen incision 3) Classical uterine incision … A) A straight transverse skin incision higher on the abdomen with blunt dissection, less pain and less blood loss B) A curved transverse skin incision with a curved fascial cut and more dissection C) A vertical incision in the upper uterine segment, used for an anterior placenta or a very preterm lower segment
questions.exp: Joel-Cohen and Pfannenstiel are abdominal wall choices; the classical uterine incision is reserved because it rules out a future trial of labour. (Book p563)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: A 27-year-old woman with one previous LSCS at 34 weeks for fetal distress is now 38 weeks, cephalic, with adequate pelvis and no contraindication. She asks about options and success rates. What do you counsel?
opts: Trial of labour succeeds in about 70% or elective repeat caesarean at 39 weeks; avoid prostaglandins
Trial of labour succeeds in about 30% or elective repeat caesarean at 34 weeks with steroids
Elective repeat caesarean at 36 weeks only, since trial of labour is never offered after a scar
Induction with prostaglandins at 38 weeks followed by trial of labour in every woman with a scar
questions.exp: A trial of scar succeeds in roughly seven out of ten women; prostaglandins are avoided because they raise the rupture risk. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: All of the following are increased risks associated with trial of labour after caesarean EXCEPT:
opts: Bleeding, need for transfusion, uterine rupture, hysterectomy and fetal distress or death
Transient tachypnoea of the newborn from delayed clearance of fetal lung fluid after caesarean
Severe perineal trauma and anal sphincter injury from vaginal delivery after previous scar
Post-term pregnancy and meconium aspiration syndrome unrelated to mode of delivery
questions.exp: A trial of labour trades anaesthetic and respiratory risk for rupture, haemorrhage and intrapartum fetal compromise. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: All of the following are recognised risks of elective repeat caesarean EXCEPT:
opts: Transient tachypnoea of the newborn, operative and anaesthetic risks and impact on future pregnancies
Uterine rupture in labour and hypoxic-ischaemic encephalopathy from obstructed labour
Severe perineal trauma, pelvic floor dysfunction and anal sphincter injury after vaginal birth
Shoulder dystocia and Erb's palsy from vaginal delivery of a macrosomic fetus
questions.exp: Elective caesarean raises neonatal respiratory morbidity and complicates later pregnancies; it protects against perineal trauma and shoulder dystocia. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Which of the following statements about risk of scar rupture after caesarean is TRUE?
opts: Rupture risk depends on type of previous incision, number of previous caesareans and inter-delivery interval
Rupture risk depends on maternal age alone, which determines tensile strength of the uterine scar
Rupture risk depends on fetal sex and birth weight, since a large baby stretches the scar in labour
Rupture risk depends on placental site alone, because a fundal placenta weakens the lower segment
questions.exp: Rupture risk tracks the scar itself — a classical scar, multiple scars and a short inter-delivery interval all raise it. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Fill up: Ideal inter-delivery interval after caesarean is ______ months; short interval is ______ months; minimum conception gap is ______ months.
questions.exp: Ideal ≥18 months; short = 12 months; minimum CS-to-conception gap 6 months. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: Fill up: Anaesthesia level for painless labour is ______ and for caesarean section is ______.
opts: L1; T6
S2; T8
questions.exp: Labour epidural T10; caesarean T4. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: A 26-year-old woman is posted for elective caesarean at 39 weeks for breech presentation. Anaesthetist asks about ideal positioning to prevent supine hypotension. What is the ideal position and timing for non-medical elective CS?
opts: Supine with 15° left lateral tilt; elective caesarean at 39 weeks for non-medical reasons
Supine with 15° left lateral tilt; elective caesarean at 37 weeks to avoid labour onset
Lithotomy position with pelvic wedge; elective caesarean at 39 weeks after lung maturity
Right lateral tilt with wedge under hip; elective caesarean at 40 weeks beyond expected date
questions.exp: The ideal position for caesarean is supine with 15° left lateral tilt or a wedge under the right hip, and elective caesarean for non-medical reasons is timed at 39 weeks. (Book p564)

questions.sec: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
questions.q: A woman with one previous lower-segment caesarean section for fetal distress is at 39 weeks with a singleton cephalic fetus of estimated weight 3.4 kg and no other risk factors. How should she be counselled?
opts: Offer a trial of labour after caesarean, since about seven in ten women succeed and the risk of uterine rupture is low
Insist on an elective repeat caesarean, because a trial of labour is never safe after a scar
Recommend induction with prostaglandins, which improves the chance of vaginal birth
Advise a home birth, since a previous lower segment scar needs no monitoring
questions.exp: With one previous low transverse scar the success rate is around 70-75 per cent and rupture risk under one per cent, but prostaglandins are avoided. (Book p564)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: All of the following are absolute contraindications to VBAC EXCEPT:
opts: Past history of CPD alone without current contracted pelvis or other scar complications
Previous classical caesarean, prior uterine rupture, myomectomy entering cavity or T-shaped incision
Contracted pelvis or cephalopelvic disproportion in the present pregnancy on clinical pelvimetry
Home delivery setting with no facility for emergency caesarean section or blood transfusion
questions.exp: Past h/o CPD is NOT a C/I; the others are. A T-shaped incision extends from LUS into upper segment. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Relative contraindications where repeat CS is preferred:
opts: Macrosomia, post-term pregnancy, and malpresentation such as breech
Twin pregnancy, polyhydramnios, and a previous caesarean section
A previous vaginal delivery and a low transverse uterine scar
Maternal age above 30 and a short interdelivery interval
questions.exp: Relative contraindications where repeat caesarean is preferred are macrosomia, post-term pregnancy and malpresentation such as breech. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Fill up: The most important favourable marker for VBAC is ______ and a bad marker is ______.
opts: previous vaginal delivery; previous puerperal sepsis in the scar
young maternal age; macrosomic fetus in present pregnancy
male fetus; twin pregnancy in present gestation
short maternal stature; post-term pregnancy beyond 40 weeks
questions.exp: Previous vaginal delivery, especially after a caesarean, predicts success; infection in the uterine scar predicts failure and rupture. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Monitoring during VBAC includes:
opts: Maternal pulse rate, CTG monitoring, scar tenderness
Serial USG for scar thickness every hour
Urine output only
Blood pressure every 4 hours
questions.exp: Pulse, CTG, scar tenderness. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: All of the following contraindicate a trial of labour after caesarean EXCEPT:
opts: A single previous low transverse incision in the lower segment
A previous classical or T-shaped uterine incision
Previous uterine rupture or full-thickness myomectomy
Placenta previa or placenta accreta spectrum in the current pregnancy
questions.exp: One previous low transverse scar is the prerequisite for offering a trial of labour; upper segment scars and placental obstruction are contraindications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: A 29-year-old woman with one previous LSCS at 38 weeks presents at 39 weeks with Bishop score 4. She desires VBAC and needs induction. What is the recommended method for induction in previous caesarean?
opts: Mechanical cervical ripening with Foley followed by oxytocin; prostaglandins are avoided
Misoprostol 25 mcg vaginally for ripening; oxytocin is avoided due to rupture risk
Dinoprostone gel for cervical ripening; mechanical methods are avoided in scarred uterus
Induction is never attempted after caesarean, so elective repeat caesarean is always performed
questions.exp: Induction of labour in a previous C-section is done by a mechanical method for cervical ripening followed by oxytocin; prostaglandins are avoided. (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Match the procedure with its status in previous caesarean — 1) External cephalic version 2) Internal podalic version 3) Contracted pelvis … A) Relative contraindication B) Absolute contraindication C) Recurrent indication for caesarean
questions.exp: External version relative C/I; internal podalic version absolute C/I; contracted pelvis is a recurrent CS indication. (Book p566)

questions.sec: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
questions.q: Increased complications after caesarean include:
opts: Transient tachypnea of newborn and postpartum endometritis
Neonatal hypoglycemia and mastitis
Cord prolapse and PPH
Erb's palsy and fistula
questions.exp: TTN and postpartum endometritis. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: All of the following are indications for classical caesarean section (difficult lower segment access) EXCEPT:
opts: Carcinoma cervix, dense bladder adhesions and placenta previa with large vessels over lower segment
Breech presentation, uncomplicated twin pregnancy and macrosomic fetus at term without obstruction
One previous lower segment scar alone with no other complicating factor in present pregnancy
Fetal distress at term and failed induction of labour where lower segment is accessible
questions.exp: Classical section is chosen when the lower segment cannot be reached or entered safely, not for the usual obstetric indications. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Perimortem caesarean section should be performed within:
opts: 4 minutes
10 minutes
30 minutes
1 minute
questions.exp: Perimortem CS within 4 minutes. (Book p565)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: M/c anaesthesia for caesarean and the preferred option in heart disease/PIH:
opts: Spinal anaesthesia; neuraxial > epidural anaesthesia
General anaesthesia; spinal
Epidural; general
Local infiltration; spinal
questions.exp: Spinal is m/c; heart disease and PIH → neuraxial/epidural. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
questions.q: Indications for general anaesthesia in caesarean/obstetric procedures:
opts: Fetal distress, convulsions, and manoeuvres that need a hand inside the uterus, such as manual removal of the placenta
Elective caesarean at 39 weeks, an uncomplicated placenta previa and one previous lower segment scar
Maternal heart disease, pregnancy-induced hypertension and an uncomplicated twin pregnancy
Prolonged labour, maternal request for sterilisation and a previous spinal anaesthetic
questions.exp: General anaesthesia is needed when speed matters or when the procedure needs uterine relaxation and a hand inside the uterus. (Book p566)

questions.sec: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia
questions.q: Fill up: In a perimortem caesarean section the baby should be delivered within ______ minutes of maternal cardiac arrest, through a ______ abdominal incision.
opts: 4; midline vertical
5; Pfannenstiel
4; Pfannenstiel
10; midline vertical
questions.exp: Delivery within four minutes improves both neonatal survival and maternal venous return, so a fast midline vertical incision is used. (Book p566)

units.title: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section
units.guide: Place the Pfannenstiel and Joel-Cohen incisions, weigh transverse-incision pros and cons, and compare Sanger's, Kerr's and Krönig's uterine incisions by rupture risk and VBAC eligibility. Focus for this checkpoint: Skin & uterine incisions for caesarean section.

units.title: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section
units.guide: Choose between TOLAC and repeat section, list the risks of each path, and master the inter-delivery interval numbers and anaesthesia levels. Focus for this checkpoint: Previous caesarean: trial of labour vs repeat section.

units.title: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring
units.guide: Separate absolute from relative contraindications to VBAC, remember what is NOT a contraindication, identify prognostic markers and monitor the scar. Focus for this checkpoint: VBAC: contraindications, prognosis & monitoring.

units.title: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean
units.guide: Know when the lower segment cannot be used, the 4-minute perimortem rule, and match spinal, epidural and general anaesthesia to their indications. Focus for this checkpoint: Classical caesarean indications & anaesthesia for caesarean.
